problems.title: Count Digits
problems.statement: Count how many digits are in a given integer. Input: a single integer n.

problems.title: Reverse Integer
problems.statement: Reverse the digits of a signed 32-bit integer, returning 0 if the result overflows. Input: a single integer x (may be negative).

problems.title: Palindrome Number
problems.statement: Determine whether an integer reads the same forwards and backwards, without converting it to a string. Input: a single integer x.

problems.title: GCD / HCF of Two Numbers
problems.statement: Find the greatest common divisor of two integers using the Euclidean algorithm. Input: two integers a and b, space-separated.

problems.title: Armstrong Numbers
problems.statement: Check whether a number equals the sum of its own digits, each raised to the power of the digit count. Input: a single integer n.

problems.title: Print All Divisors of a Number
problems.statement: List every divisor of a given number in O(sqrt(n)) time by checking divisor pairs. Input: a single integer n. Output all its divisors sorted ascending, space-separated.

problems.title: Check for Prime Number
problems.statement: Determine whether a number is prime by testing divisibility up to its square root. Input: a single integer n.

problems.title: Count Primes (Sieve of Eratosthenes)
problems.statement: Count how many prime numbers exist below a given bound, using the Sieve of Eratosthenes instead of testing each number individually. Input: a single integer n. Count primes strictly less than n.

problems.title: Pow(x, n)
problems.statement: Compute x raised to the integer power n in logarithmic time using fast exponentiation. Input: a real number x, then an integer n, space-separated. Output the result rounded to exactly 5 decimal places.

problems.title: Recursive Sum of First N Numbers
problems.statement: Compute the sum 1 + 2 + ... + N using recursion instead of a loop. Input: a single integer n. Output 1+2+...+n.

problems.title: Factorial of a Number
problems.statement: Compute N! recursively, multiplying N by the factorial of N-1. Input: a single integer n.

problems.title: Fibonacci Number
problems.statement: Compute the nth Fibonacci number, where each number is the sum of the two before it. Input: a single integer n (0-indexed: F(0)=0, F(1)=1).

problems.title: Print Right Triangle
problems.statement: Print a right-aligned-at-the-left triangle of stars with n rows. Row i (1-indexed, i from 1 to n) contains exactly i stars, with no spaces between them. Input: a single integer n (1 <= n <= 9). Output: the pattern for that n, one row per line, using exactly the spacing described above -- no trailing spaces on any line.
problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra (O(n) for the printed output itself)
hints: Use two nested loops: the outer loop picks the row, the inner loop prints that row's stars.
Row i needs exactly i stars -- the inner loop should run from 1 to i.

problems.title: Print Inverted Right Triangle
problems.statement: Print the mirror image of the right triangle: it starts wide and narrows to a point. Row i (1-indexed) contains (n - i + 1) stars, with no spaces between them. Input: a single integer n (1 <= n <= 9). Output: the pattern for that n, one row per line, using exactly the spacing described above -- no trailing spaces on any line.
problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra (O(n) for the printed output itself)
hints: The first row has the most stars (n), and each following row has one fewer.
Row i needs (n - i + 1) stars.

problems.title: Print Pyramid
problems.statement: Print a centered pyramid of stars. Row i (1-indexed) has (n - i) leading spaces, followed by (2*i - 1) stars, with no spaces between the stars themselves. Input: a single integer n (1 <= n <= 9). Output: the pattern for that n, one row per line, using exactly the spacing described above -- no trailing spaces on any line.
problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra (O(n) for the printed output itself)
hints: Each row needs leading spaces to center the stars under the row below it.
Row i needs (n - i) spaces followed by (2*i - 1) stars.

problems.title: Print Inverted Pyramid
problems.statement: Print the pyramid upside down: wide at the top, a single star at the bottom. Row i (1-indexed) has (i - 1) leading spaces, followed by (2*(n - i) + 1) stars, with no spaces between the stars themselves. Input: a single integer n (1 <= n <= 9). Output: the pattern for that n, one row per line, using exactly the spacing described above -- no trailing spaces on any line.
problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra (O(n) for the printed output itself)
hints: This is the pyramid pattern with the rows visited in reverse order.
Row i needs (i - 1) leading spaces and (2*(n - i) + 1) stars.

problems.title: Print Diamond
problems.statement: Print a diamond made of stars: a pyramid on top of an inverted pyramid, sharing no duplicated middle row. First print the pyramid pattern for rows 1..n (row i: (n - i) leading spaces + (2*i - 1) stars), then print the same formula for rows (n-1) down to 1. Input: a single integer n (1 <= n <= 9). Output: the pattern for that n, one row per line, using exactly the spacing described above -- no trailing spaces on any line.
problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra (O(n) for the printed output itself)
hints: Build it as two halves: the pyramid pattern going down, then the same row formula going back up (skipping the widest row a second time).
The total number of rows is (2*n - 1).

problems.title: Print Hourglass
problems.statement: Print an hourglass made of stars: wide at the top and bottom, narrowing to a point in the middle. First print the inverted-pyramid formula for rows 1..n (row i: (i - 1) leading spaces + (2*(n - i) + 1) stars), then print the same formula for rows (n-1) down to 1. Input: a single integer n (1 <= n <= 9). Output: the pattern for that n, one row per line, using exactly the spacing described above -- no trailing spaces on any line.
problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra (O(n) for the printed output itself)
hints: This is the mirror image of the diamond pattern -- narrow in the middle instead of the ends.
Reuse the inverted-pyramid row formula for both halves.

problems.title: Print Number Triangle
problems.statement: Print a right triangle where each row counts up from 1. Row i (1-indexed) contains the digits 1 through i, concatenated with no separators (n stays small enough that every value is a single digit). Input: a single integer n (1 <= n <= 9). Output: the pattern for that n, one row per line, using exactly the spacing described above -- no trailing spaces on any line.
problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra (O(n) for the printed output itself)
hints: Same shape as the right triangle of stars, but print numbers 1..i instead of i stars.
Loop the inner counter from 1 to i and print it directly.

problems.title: Print Repeated Number Triangle
problems.statement: Print a right triangle where every star in a row is replaced by that row's own number. Row i (1-indexed) contains the digit i repeated i times, concatenated with no separators. Input: a single integer n (1 <= n <= 9). Output: the pattern for that n, one row per line, using exactly the spacing described above -- no trailing spaces on any line.
problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra (O(n) for the printed output itself)
hints: This is the right triangle of stars, but every star becomes the row number instead.
Row i is just the digit i printed i times in a row.

problems.title: Print Numeric Palindromic Triangle
problems.statement: Print a right triangle of numbers that count up then back down within each row. Row i (1-indexed) contains the digits 1..i followed by the digits (i-1)..1, all concatenated with no separators (e.g. row 3 is "12321"). Input: a single integer n (1 <= n <= 9). Output: the pattern for that n, one row per line, using exactly the spacing described above -- no trailing spaces on any line.
problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra (O(n) for the printed output itself)
hints: Each row is symmetric: it counts up to i, then immediately counts back down to 1 without repeating i.
Build the ascending half (1..i) and the descending half (i-1..1) and concatenate them.

problems.title: Print Centered Numeric Pyramid
problems.statement: Print the numeric palindromic triangle, but centered like a pyramid instead of left-aligned. Row i (1-indexed) has (n - i) leading spaces, followed by the digits 1..i then (i-1)..1 concatenated with no separators. Input: a single integer n (1 <= n <= 9). Output: the pattern for that n, one row per line, using exactly the spacing described above -- no trailing spaces on any line.
problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra (O(n) for the printed output itself)
hints: Combine the pyramid's leading-space formula with the numeric palindromic triangle's row content.
Row i needs (n - i) leading spaces before the "1..i..1" digits.

problems.title: Print Hollow Square
problems.statement: Print an n x n square outline made of stars, hollow on the inside. The first and last rows are n stars with no spaces. Every row in between starts and ends with a star, with (n - 2) plain spaces in between. Input: a single integer n (1 <= n <= 9). Output: the pattern for that n, one row per line, using exactly the spacing described above -- no trailing spaces on any line.
problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra (O(n) for the printed output itself)
hints: Only the border needs to be filled in -- the first row, the last row, and the first/last character of every row in between.
A middle row is: one star, (n - 2) spaces, one star.

problems.title: Print Butterfly Pattern
problems.statement: Print a butterfly made of stars: two triangles that meet in the middle, mirrored top and bottom. Upper half, row i (1-indexed, i from 1 to n): i stars, then 2*(n - i) spaces, then i stars. Lower half repeats the same formula for rows (n-1) down to 1. Input: a single integer n (1 <= n <= 9). Output: the pattern for that n, one row per line, using exactly the spacing described above -- no trailing spaces on any line.
problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra (O(n) for the printed output itself)
hints: Each row (top or bottom half) has the same shape: stars, a gap that shrinks toward the middle, then matching stars.
Row i's gap width is 2*(n - i) spaces; the bottom half reuses the same formula in reverse row order.

problems.title: Selection Sort
problems.statement: Repeatedly select the minimum remaining element and move it to the front of the unsorted part of the array. Input: the array, space-separated. Output it sorted ascending, space-separated.

problems.title: Bubble Sort
problems.statement: Repeatedly swap adjacent out-of-order elements until the array is sorted. Input: the array, space-separated. Output it sorted ascending, space-separated.

problems.title: Insertion Sort
problems.statement: Build the sorted array one element at a time by inserting each new element into its correct position. Input: the array, space-separated. Output it sorted ascending, space-separated.

problems.title: Merge Sort
problems.statement: Recursively split the array in half, sort each half, and merge the sorted halves back together. Input: the array, space-separated. Output it sorted ascending, space-separated.

problems.title: Quick Sort
problems.statement: Partition the array around a pivot so smaller elements land left and larger ones right, then recursively sort each side. Input: the array, space-separated. Output it sorted ascending, space-separated.

problems.title: Sort Colors (Dutch National Flag)
problems.statement: Sort an array containing only 0s, 1s, and 2s in a single pass using three pointers. Input: the array of 0/1/2 values, space-separated. Output it sorted ascending, space-separated.

problems.title: Largest Element in an Array
problems.statement: Find the maximum value in an array in a single pass. Input: the array, space-separated.

problems.title: Second Largest Element in an Array
problems.statement: Find the second-largest distinct value in an array without sorting it. Input: the array, space-separated. Output the second largest distinct value, or -1 if none exists.

problems.title: Check if an Array Is Sorted
problems.statement: Determine whether an array is sorted in non-decreasing order. Input: the array, space-separated. Output whether it's sorted in non-decreasing order.

problems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
problems.statement: Remove duplicates in place from a sorted array and return the count of unique elements. Input: a sorted array, space-separated. Output the distinct values in order, space-separated.

problems.title: Left Rotate an Array by One Place
problems.statement: Shift every element one position to the left, wrapping the first element around to the end. Input: the array, space-separated.

problems.title: Rotate Array
problems.statement: Rotate an array to the right by k steps, in place. Input: the array, then k on the next line. Rotate the array right by k steps.

problems.title: Move Zeroes
problems.statement: Move all zeroes in an array to the end while keeping the relative order of the other elements. Input: the array, space-separated. Move all zeroes to the end, keeping the relative order of the non-zero values.

problems.title: Linear Search
problems.statement: Find the index of a target value by scanning the array from the start. Input: the array, then the target on the next line. Output the 0-indexed position of target, or -1 if absent.

problems.title: Union of Two Sorted Arrays
problems.statement: Merge two sorted arrays into one sorted array containing only the distinct values from both. Input: two sorted arrays, one per line, space-separated. Output their sorted union with duplicates removed, space-separated.

problems.title: Missing Number
problems.statement: Given an array containing n distinct numbers from 0 to n, find the one number missing from the range. Input: the array, space-separated (n distinct values from 0..n with one missing).

problems.title: Max Consecutive Ones
problems.statement: Find the length of the longest run of consecutive 1s in a binary array. Input: the array of 0/1 values, space-separated.

problems.title: Single Number
problems.statement: Every element appears twice except one — find that single element in linear time and constant space. Input: the array, space-separated (every value appears twice except one).

problems.title: Longest Subarray with Sum K (positives)
problems.statement: Find the length of the longest subarray of positive integers whose elements sum to exactly K. Input: the array (all positive values), then k on the next line. Output the length of the longest contiguous subarray summing to k.

problems.title: Two Sum
problems.statement: Given an array of integers and a target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to the target. Input: the array, then the target on the next line. Output the two 0-indexed positions (any valid pair), space-separated, ascending.

problems.title: Majority Element
problems.statement: Find the element that appears more than n/2 times in an array. Input: the array, space-separated (a majority element is guaranteed to exist).

problems.title: Maximum Subarray
problems.statement: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum. Input: the array, space-separated.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.statement: Given daily stock prices, find the maximum profit from buying on one day and selling on a later day. Input: the daily prices, space-separated. Output the maximum achievable profit (0 if none possible).

problems.title: Rearrange Array Elements by Sign
problems.statement: Rearrange an array with an equal number of positive and negative values so the signs alternate, starting with a positive. Input: the array, space-separated (equal counts of positive and negative values). Output the rearranged array, positive first, alternating, preserving each sign's relative order.

problems.title: Next Permutation
problems.statement: Rearrange numbers into the lexicographically next greater permutation, or the lowest order if none exists. Input: the array, space-separated. Output the next permutation, space-separated.

problems.title: Leaders in an Array
problems.statement: Find every element that is greater than all elements to its right. Input: the array, space-separated. Output the leaders in the order they appear, space-separated (the last element is always a leader).

problems.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
problems.statement: Find the length of the longest run of consecutive integers in an unsorted array, in linear time. Input: the array, space-separated.

problems.title: Set Matrix Zeroes
problems.statement: If an element in a matrix is 0, set its entire row and column to 0, in place. Input: rows and cols on the first line, then that many rows of space-separated integers. Output the resulting matrix in the same format (rows and cols line, then the rows).

problems.title: Rotate Image
problems.statement: Rotate an n x n matrix 90 degrees clockwise, in place. Input: n, then n rows of space-separated integers. Output the rotated matrix, n rows of space-separated integers.

problems.title: Spiral Matrix
problems.statement: Return all elements of a matrix in spiral order. Input: rows and cols on the first line, then that many rows of space-separated integers. Output all elements in spiral order, space-separated.

problems.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
problems.statement: Count the number of contiguous subarrays whose sum equals K. Input: the array, then k on the next line. Output the count of contiguous subarrays summing to k.

problems.title: Pascal's Triangle
problems.statement: Generate the first n rows of Pascal's triangle, where each number is the sum of the two above it. Input: n (number of rows). Output n lines, row i (0-indexed) containing its space-separated values.

problems.title: Majority Element II
problems.statement: Find every element that appears more than n/3 times in an array. Input: the array, space-separated. Output every element appearing more than n/3 times, ascending, space-separated (there are at most two).

problems.title: 3Sum
problems.statement: Find all unique triplets in an array that sum to zero. Input: the array, space-separated. Output each unique triplet summing to zero, one per line, values ascending within the triplet, triplets sorted lexicographically.

problems.title: 4Sum
problems.statement: Find all unique quadruplets in an array that sum to a given target. Input: the array, then the target on the next line. Output each unique quadruplet summing to target, one per line, values ascending within the quadruplet, quadruplets sorted lexicographically.

problems.title: Largest Subarray with 0 Sum
problems.statement: Find the length of the longest subarray whose elements sum to zero. Input: the array, space-separated. Output the length of the longest subarray summing to zero.

problems.title: Count Subarrays with Given XOR K
problems.statement: Count the number of subarrays whose elements XOR together to exactly K. Input: the array, then k on the next line. Output the count of subarrays whose XOR equals k.

problems.title: Merge Intervals
problems.statement: Merge all overlapping intervals in a collection into a minimal set of non-overlapping intervals. Input: n, then n lines of "start end". Output the merged intervals, one per line as "start end", sorted by start.

problems.title: Merge Sorted Array
problems.statement: Merge a sorted array into another sorted array that has enough trailing space to hold both, in place. Input: the first sorted array's real values, then the second sorted array's values, each space-separated on its own line. Output the merged sorted array, space-separated.

problems.title: Find the Repeating and Missing Number
problems.statement: In an array of 1 to n with one number repeated and one missing, find both. Input: the array, space-separated (values 1..n, one repeated once, one missing). Output the repeating value then the missing value, space-separated.

problems.title: Count Inversions
problems.statement: Count the number of pairs (i, j) where i < j but arr[i] > arr[j]. Input: the array, space-separated. Output the count of inversions.

problems.title: Reverse Pairs
problems.statement: Count the number of pairs (i, j) where i < j and arr[i] > 2 * arr[j]. Input: the array, space-separated. Output the count of such pairs.

problems.title: Maximum Product Subarray
problems.statement: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest product. Input: the array, space-separated.

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.statement: Find the index of a target value in a sorted array. Input: the array (sorted, ascending), then the target on the next line. Output the 0-indexed position of target, or -1 if absent.

problems.title: Search Insert Position
problems.statement: Find the index where a target would be inserted into a sorted array to keep it sorted. Input: the array (sorted, ascending), then the target on the next line. Output the index where target is or would be inserted.

problems.title: Find First and Last Position of Element
problems.statement: Find the first and last index of a target value in a sorted array. Input: the array (sorted, ascending), then the target on the next line. Output the first and last index of target, space-separated, or "-1 -1" if absent.

problems.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problems.statement: Find a target's index in a sorted array that has been rotated at an unknown pivot. Input: the rotated sorted array (distinct values), then the target on the next line. Output the 0-indexed position of target, or -1 if absent.

problems.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array II
problems.statement: Same as searching a rotated sorted array, but the array may contain duplicates. Input: the rotated sorted array (may contain duplicates), then the target on the next line. Output "true" if target exists, else "false".

problems.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
problems.statement: Find the minimum element in a sorted array that has been rotated at an unknown pivot. Input: the rotated sorted array (distinct values), space-separated.

problems.title: Find How Many Times an Array Has Been Rotated
problems.statement: Find how many positions a sorted array has been rotated by, by locating its minimum element. Input: the rotated sorted array (distinct values), space-separated. Output the number of rotations (the index of the minimum element).

problems.title: Single Element in a Sorted Array
problems.statement: Every element in a sorted array appears twice except one — find it in logarithmic time. Input: the sorted array where every value appears twice except one, space-separated.

problems.title: Find Peak Element
problems.statement: Find an index where the value is greater than both neighbors (values outside the array count as -infinity). Input: the array, space-separated. Output the index of the peak.

problems.title: Sqrt(x)
problems.statement: Compute the integer square root of a non-negative integer without using a built-in power function. Input: a single non-negative integer x. Output floor(sqrt(x)).

problems.title: Nth Root of a Number
problems.statement: Find the integer nth root of a number using binary search. Input: n and m on one line, space-separated. Output the integer nth root of m, or -1 if none exists exactly.

problems.title: Koko Eating Bananas
problems.statement: Find the minimum eating speed that lets Koko finish all banana piles within h hours. Input: the pile sizes, then h on the next line. Output the minimum integer eating speed.

problems.title: Minimum Days to Make M Bouquets
problems.statement: Find the minimum number of days to wait before M bouquets of K adjacent flowers can be made. Input: the bloom-day array, then m and k on the next line. Output the minimum number of days, or -1 if impossible.

problems.title: Smallest Divisor Given a Threshold
problems.statement: Find the smallest divisor such that dividing every array element by it and summing the results stays at or below a threshold. Input: the array, then the threshold on the next line. Output the smallest such divisor.

problems.title: Capacity to Ship Packages Within D Days
problems.statement: Find the minimum ship capacity that lets all packages be shipped within D days, in order. Input: the package weights, then D on the next line. Output the minimum ship capacity.

problems.title: Kth Missing Positive Number
problems.statement: Find the kth positive integer missing from a strictly increasing array. Input: the strictly increasing array, then k on the next line. Output the kth missing positive integer.

problems.title: Aggressive Cows
problems.statement: Place cows in stalls to maximize the minimum distance between any two cows. Input: the stall positions, then the number of cows c on the next line. Output the maximum possible minimum distance.

problems.title: Book Allocation Problem
problems.statement: Allocate books to students so the maximum number of pages assigned to any one student is minimized. Input: the pages array, then the number of students m on the next line. Output the minimum possible maximum pages, or -1 if m exceeds the number of books.

problems.title: Split Array Largest Sum
problems.statement: Split an array into m subarrays to minimize the largest sum among them. Input: the array, then m on the next line. Output the minimized largest subarray sum.

problems.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
problems.statement: Find the median of two sorted arrays in logarithmic time. Input: the two sorted arrays, one per line, space-separated. Output the median, printed as an integer when it has no fractional part, otherwise with exactly one decimal place.

problems.title: Row with Maximum Number of 1s
problems.statement: Find the row with the most 1s in a binary matrix whose rows are each sorted. Input: rows and cols on the first line, then that many rows of space-separated 0/1 values (each row sorted ascending). Output the 0-indexed row with the most 1s (the first such row if tied), or -1 if no row contains a 1.

problems.title: Search a 2D Matrix
problems.statement: Search for a target in a matrix where each row is sorted and the first element of each row is greater than the last element of the previous row. Input: rows and cols on the first line, then that many rows of space-separated integers, then the target on its own line. Output "true" if target exists, else "false".

problems.title: Search a 2D Matrix II
problems.statement: Search for a target in a matrix where every row and column is sorted independently. Input: rows and cols on the first line, then that many rows of space-separated integers, then the target on its own line. Output "true" if target exists, else "false".

problems.title: Find a Peak Element II
problems.statement: Find a peak element in a 2D grid, where a peak is greater than all four of its neighbors (out-of-grid neighbors count as -infinity). Input: rows and cols on the first line, then that many rows of space-separated integers. Output the row and column (0-indexed, space-separated) of the peak.

problems.title: Median in a Row-Wise Sorted Matrix
problems.statement: Find the median of all elements in a matrix whose rows are individually sorted. Input: rows and cols on the first line, then that many rows of space-separated integers (each row individually sorted ascending, total element count is odd). Output the median of all elements.

problems.title: Remove Outermost Parentheses
problems.statement: Remove the outermost parentheses of every primitive substring in a valid parentheses string. Input: one line, the parentheses string. Output: one line, the resulting string (empty line if it becomes empty).

problems.title: Reverse Words in a String
problems.statement: Reverse the order of the words in a string, collapsing extra whitespace. Input: one line, the string (may have leading/trailing/multiple spaces). Output: one line, the words reversed and single-spaced.

problems.title: Largest Odd Number in String
problems.statement: Find the largest odd-valued substring that starts from index 0 of a digit string. Input: one line, the digit string. Output: one line, the largest odd-valued prefix substring (empty line if none).

problems.title: Longest Common Prefix
problems.statement: Find the longest string that is a prefix of every string in an array. Input: n on the first line, then n lines each containing one string. Output: one line, the longest common prefix (empty line if none).

problems.title: Isomorphic Strings
problems.statement: Determine whether the characters in one string can be consistently replaced to get another string. Input: two lines, s then t. Output: one line, "true" or "false".

problems.title: Rotate String
problems.statement: Determine whether one string can become another by rotating its characters. Input: two lines, s then goal. Output: one line, "true" or "false".

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.statement: Determine whether one string is an anagram of another. Input: two lines, s then t. Output: one line, "true" or "false".

problems.title: Sort Characters by Frequency
problems.statement: Sort the characters of a string in decreasing order of frequency (choose a string with no frequency ties for the test cases so the order is unambiguous). Input: one line, the string. Output: one line, the characters sorted by decreasing frequency.

problems.title: Maximum Nesting Depth of Parentheses
problems.statement: Find the maximum depth of nested parentheses in a valid parentheses string. Input: one line, the string. Output: one line, the maximum depth as an integer.

problems.title: Roman to Integer
problems.statement: Convert a Roman numeral string to its integer value. Input: one line, the Roman numeral. Output: one line, the integer value.

problems.title: Integer to Roman
problems.statement: Convert an integer (1 to 3999) to its Roman numeral representation. Input: one line, the integer. Output: one line, the Roman numeral.

problems.title: String to Integer (atoi)
problems.statement: Implement a function that parses a leading integer out of a string, handling sign, whitespace, and overflow like the C atoi function. Input: one line, the raw string. Output: one line, the parsed integer, clamped to the signed 32-bit range [-2147483648, 2147483647] (0 if no valid integer prefix exists).

problems.title: Count Number of Substrings with K Distinct Characters
problems.statement: Count the substrings of a string that contain exactly K distinct characters. Input: the string on the first line, K on the second line. Output: one line, the count as an integer.

problems.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
problems.statement: Find the longest substring that reads the same forwards and backwards. If more than one substring of the maximum length exists, use the one whose start index is smallest (leftmost). Input: one line, the string. Output: one line, the longest palindromic substring.

problems.title: Sum of Beauty of All Substrings
problems.statement: For every substring, define its beauty as the difference between the most and least frequent character counts within it, and sum that beauty over all substrings. Input: one line, the string. Output: one line, the total sum as an integer.

problems.title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String
problems.statement: Find the index of the first occurrence of a needle string within a haystack string (-1 if not found). Input: two lines, haystack then needle. Output: one line, the index as an integer.

problems.title: Reverse Linked List

problems.statement: Find the area of the largest square containing only 1s in a binary matrix. Input: rows and cols on the first line, then that many rows of space-separated 0/1 values.

problems.title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
problems.statement: Design a trie that supports inserting a word, searching for an exact word, and checking whether any word starts with a given prefix. Input: the number of operations k, then k lines each "insert word", "search word", or "startsWith prefix". Output one line per search/startsWith operation, "true" or "false" (insert produces no output).

testCases.input:
6
insert apple
search apple
search app
startsWith app
insert app
search app

problems.title: Implement Trie II (Prefix Tree)
problems.statement: Extend a trie to also count how many inserted words equal, or start with, a given prefix, and support erasing a previously inserted word. Input: the number of operations k, then k lines each "insert word", "countWordsEqualTo word", "countWordsStartingWith prefix", or "erase word". Output one line per countWordsEqualTo/countWordsStartingWith operation, the count as an integer (insert/erase produce no output).

testCases.input:
7
insert apple
insert apple
countWordsEqualTo apple
countWordsStartingWith app
erase apple
countWordsEqualTo apple
countWordsStartingWith app

problems.title: Longest Word with All Prefixes
problems.statement: Find the longest word in a list such that every proper prefix of it is also present in the list (a single-character word always qualifies). If there's a tie in length, pick the lexicographically smallest. Input: n on the first line, then n lines each a word. Output: one line, the longest qualifying word (empty line if none, though a single-character word in the list always qualifies).

problems.title: Number of Distinct Substrings in a String
problems.statement: Count the number of distinct substrings of a string using a trie, including the empty substring. Input: one line, the string. Output: one line, the count as an integer.

problems.title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
problems.statement: Find the maximum XOR value obtainable from any two numbers in an array. Input: n on the first line, then n space-separated numbers on the second line. Output: one line, the maximum XOR as an integer.

problems.title: Maximum XOR With an Element from Array
problems.statement: For each of several queries (x, limit), find the maximum XOR obtainable by pairing x with an array element no greater than limit (-1 if no such element exists). Input: n on the first line, then n space-separated array numbers on the next line, then q on the next line, then q lines each "x limit". Output: one line per query, the answer as an integer.
